BLOCKED before driver implementation: the pinned MiniRys ROS 2 stack is an R2 mobile base but exposes no ROS-accessible acknowledged stop service or action, so an honest RosDriver safety binding cannot be declared. The only source in the clone that consumes steering is the separate rys_executor package: src/rys_base/executor/src/main.cpp:441 subscribes to /rys/control/steering with rys_interfaces/msg/Steering; the callback at lines 433-439 stores throttle, rotation, precision and balancing, and the control loop applies them through calculateSpeeds and setMotorSpeeds at lines 364-368. That callback publishes no acknowledgement of applied motion or of a stopped state. The shipped rys_launch stack (src/rys_base/launch/src/main.cpp:78-84) adds only MotorsControllerNode and IMUNode; in the launched motors controller the enable/steering/battery/temperature subscriptions, odometry publisher, regulator services and loop timer are all commented out at src/rys_base/motors_controller/src/MotorsControllerNode.cpp:79-104, and only the IMU subscription at line 84 is active. The launched node therefore consumes neither /rys/control/steering nor /rys/control/enable_motors. The rys_remote GUI declares a std_msgs/Bool publisher on /rys/control/enable_motors at src/rys_remote/src/ROS/RysRemoteNode.py:24 and a Steering publisher on /rys/control/steering at line 26, but no active subscriber exists in the launched stack (the subscription is commented out at MotorsControllerNode.cpp:79), and a Bool publication would be transmission-only even if one did. The only ROS services in the executable control path are /rys/control/regulator_settings/get and /set at src/rys_base/executor/src/main.cpp:468 and :485; the setter writes six PID parameters and returns success=true and error_text='success' at lines 469-485. That is a gain-configuration service, not a stop, and it does not write zero motor speeds. The only native motor stop is MotorsController::disableMotors() at src/rys_base/executor/src/MotorsController.cpp:225-239, which writes a disabled, zero-speed PRU frame; it is called from the constructor at line 42, the destructor at line 46, and after the control thread leaves its loop on SIGINT/destruction at src/rys_base/executor/src/main.cpp:396. No ROS service or action reaches that method. README.md:17-19 leaves the MiniRys robot requirements as a TODO, and the clone contains no e-stop, emergency-stop, kill-switch or power-isolation text, so there is no source-backed estop_physical_ref. A RosDriver safety stop must be a fixed, input-free service or action (MHS/sdk/docs/ros-driver.md); a topic publication is transmission-only and a fake cannot supply a missing native stop. cap.motion.mobile_base.v1 also requires a bounded duration plus distance and heading output that the upstream Steering interface does not provide, so even the steering surface is an extension candidate; the safety gap blocks it regardless. Risk is R2 because this is a mobile base (robot.mobile_base; cap.motion.mobile_base.v1 risk_class R2), above the card floor R0. No driver.py, fake.py, facts.md, test_driver.py, driver.lock.json or reference was authored. The only gate run is the missing-layout diagnostic recorded here; it is not executable driver evidence. No hardware was attached, no ROS graph or rosbridge was contacted, and no hardware run, human review or human test is claimed.

A self-balancing mobile base with no ROS-reachable acknowledged stop is NO_HARDWARE_FREE_PATH at R2. The card needs the owner's publication decision (publish_review required; licence not stated (NOASSERTION)); the package may not be published or merged into a published tree before it. For the human reviewer: Real MiniRys hardware (BeagleBone PRU motor frames); README.md:42 says it will not work without modifications on anything other than MiniRys v3.1. The executor enables the motors at start-up and enters the balancing loop after a 20 s countdown (main.cpp:257-275); only SIGINT or destruction disables them. The rys_remote GUI republishes Steering on a timer while enabled and an enable Bool that no launched node consumes (RysRemoteNode.py:57-58, 66-84), so it competes with any other steering publisher. Licence: the clone has no LICENSE file and every package.xml has an empty license tag (card NOASSERTION, publish_review required). Unblocking needs an acknowledged stop service or action in the executor, or a physical stop the operator owns.
